Plan-review remediation for 1cf6-f902-5bfa-438f (doctoral-wandering-velvetworm)
Investigated read-only in the worktree /Users/joeoakhart/impl-2ddd-consolidation
on 2026-08-21, at HEAD 3406014085 (post-StorePaths landing).

================================================================================
WHAT WAS FACTUALLY WRONG, AND WHAT REPLACED IT
================================================================================

1. MISCOUNT: the loop exists THREE times, not twice.
   The plan named only enrich_drain and compact_trigger. A third, structurally
   identical copy lives at src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:109-145
   (_acquire_worker_lock) / :148-158 (release_worker_lock). It performs the same
   os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL create inside `for attempt in range(2)` and adjudicates
   with the same rebar._store.lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale.
   Corrected: gc_trigger.py and tests/unit/test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py added to
   Scope and Testing.

   COMMAND:
     grep -rn "stamped_file_is_stale" --include="*.py" .
   OUTPUT (production sites only):
     src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:130
     src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:128
     src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:145
     src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py:304        <- reader, not a copy
     src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:330             <- the definition

2. BOTH LINE CITATIONS WERE WRONG.
   Plan said _acquire_advisory_lock at enrich_drain.py:129-176 and
   _acquire_trigger_lock at compact_trigger.py:150-204. Neither range bounds the
   function.

   COMMAND (python ast over each file, printing lineno/end_lineno):
     src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:74-95     (22 LOC)  _describe_drain_lock_holder
     src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:98-170    (73 LOC)  _acquire_advisory_lock
     src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:173-178   (6 LOC)   _release_advisory_lock
     src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:119-160 (42 LOC) _acquire_trigger_lock
     src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:163-173 (11 LOC) release_trigger_lock
     src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:109-145 (37 LOC) _acquire_worker_lock
     src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:148-158 (11 LOC) release_worker_lock
   This also refutes "~45 LOC each": the acquire bodies are 73 / 42 / 37.

3. "STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL" WAS UNPROVEN, AND IS FALSE IN FOUR PLACES.
   Read all three implementations in full. Findings:

   (a) TIMEOUT / RECLAMATION CEILING - IDENTICAL, nothing to reconcile.
       All three call stamped_file_is_stale(path) with no extra arguments. That
       function fixes fcntl_held=False and unrecognised_via_ceiling=True
       internally (lock_owner.py:330-353) and the only ceiling in play is
       _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S = 3600 (lock_owner.py:46). Retry cap is
       range(2) in all three. So the two things a merge could most easily break
       are in fact already shared. Recorded explicitly in the plan so a reviewer
       does not have to re-derive it.

   (b) RELEASE SEMANTICS - THE ONE REAL BEHAVIOUR DELTA (highest value).
       enrich_drain.py:173-178:
           try:
               os.close(fd)
               os.unlink(_drain_lock_path(tracker))
           except OSError:
               pass
       One try block: if os.close raises, the unlink NEVER RUNS and the lock file
       leaks until the 3600 s ceiling reclaims it.
       compact_trigger.py:163-173 and gc_trigger.py:148-158 both use TWO
       independent try blocks, so the unlink always runs.
       A naive "they're the same, pick one" merge flips this silently in either
       direction. The plan now MANDATES the two-block form, states that this is a
       deliberate behaviour change to the drain, and pins it with
       test_release_unlinks_even_when_close_fails.

   (c) STAMP BYTES - differ, but provably invisible.
       enrich_drain.py:165 writes (_owner._owner_stamp() + "\n");
       compact_trigger.py:156 and gc_trigger.py:142 write no newline.
       Both readers strip: lock_owner.py:349-350 and doctor_locks.py:279-280 each
       do fh.read().strip(). Disposition: adopt the no-newline form, pin by test.

   (d) LOGGING - differs.
       Drain names the holder in its reclaim WARNING via
       _describe_drain_lock_holder (enrich_drain.py:129-134) and warns on a failed
       stamp (:167-169). The other two log a bare message
       (compact_trigger.py:147, gc_trigger.py:132) and swallow the stamp failure
       with a bare `pass`.
       The drain's holder phrasing is CONTRACTUALLY PINNED to doctor's wording:
         tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:585
           ::test_drain_and_doctor_describe_a_holderless_lock_identically
       Disposition: inject describe_holder as a callback (drain passes its helper,
       the other two pass None); adopt the drain's stamp-failure WARNING for all
       three, which is a strict logging superset.

   (e) DIRECTORY CREATION - differs three ways, so it stays with the callers.
       drain: os.makedirs(StorePaths(tracker).rebar_dir, exist_ok=True), returns
              None on OSError (enrich_drain.py:118-122)
       compaction: same shape (compact_trigger.py:135-139)
       GC: no makedirs; _gc_dir does mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) inside the
           path helper (gc_trigger.py:65-69), and the acquire only wraps the path
           call (gc_trigger.py:122-125)
       The shared helper therefore takes an already-resolved path and owns no
       directory creation. GC also passes a Path, not a str.

4. THE GUARD CRITERION AS WRITTEN COULD NOT WORK. Chose the anchor empirically.
   Original AC: grep -rn "O_EXCL" <the two files> is empty.
   Too narrow (misses gc_trigger) and, widened repo-wide, over-matches.

   EXPERIMENT 1 - bare O_EXCL, repo-wide:
     COMMAND: grep -rn "O_EXCL" --include="*.py" . | grep -v "/.git/"
     Legitimate production hits that MUST survive:
       src/rebar/_signing_hmac.py:100,104          (prose in a docstring)
       src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py:13               (prose)
       src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:122     (a real, unrelated O_EXCL create)
       src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:385   (the literal string "O_EXCL" as
                                                    a concurrency-overlay trigger token)
       src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py:49,249  (prose)
     => 7 lines. A bare O_EXCL guard would flag all of them. REJECTED.

   EXPERIMENT 2 - O_EXCL AND stamped_file_is_stale:
     COMMAND:
       grep -rln "O_EXCL" src/rebar --include="*.py" \
         | xargs grep -ln "stamped_file_is_stale"
     OUTPUT:
       src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py
       src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py
       src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py     <- FALSE POSITIVE
       src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py
     doctor_locks is the diagnostic READER: prose O_EXCL at :49,:249 and a real
     stamped_file_is_stale call at :304, while deliberately opening WITHOUT
     O_CREAT (:119). It must survive. REJECTED.

   EXPERIMENT 3 (ADOPTED) - os.O_CREAT AND stamped_file_is_stale:
     COMMAND:
       grep -rlF "os.O_CREAT" src/rebar --include="*.py" \
         | xargs grep -lF "stamped_file_is_stale" \
         | grep -v "^src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py$"
     OUTPUT (exactly the three copies, no false positives):
       src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py
       src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py
       src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py
     doctor_locks only says "O_CREAT" in prose at :119, without the os. prefix, so
     the -F literal match excludes it. This is now AC 1, and it fails on the
     current tree and passes after a correct implementation.

   Companion criterion pins the survivors:
     COMMAND: grep -c "O_EXCL" src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py \
       src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py src/rebar/_signing_hmac.py \
       src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py
     OUTPUT: 7 matches total, today and after.

5. MONKEYPATCH / STRING HAZARD not mentioned by the plan.
     COMMAND: grep -rn "_acquire_trigger_lock|release_trigger_lock" over tests/
     tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py:134:
       monkeypatch.setattr(compact_trigger, "_acquire_trigger_lock", lambda t: 3)
     tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py:135:
       monkeypatch.setattr(compact_trigger, "release_trigger_lock", lambda t, fd: None)
   Both are patched BY NAME as module attributes with NO raising=False, so if the
   consolidation removes either module-level attribute the test errors on
   attribute-not-found rather than failing informatively. Recorded as a hard
   constraint.

6. MISSING CONSUMERS.
   - rebar._commands.doctor_locks is the reader of both stamps. It keeps its own
     private copies of the lock filenames (doctor_locks.py:101-103:
     _HLC_LOCK_NAME, _DRAIN_LOCK_NAME, _COMPACT_WORKER_LOCK_NAME) and renders them
     through _existence_report (:248-317), reached from scan_locks (:320-370).
   - compact_trigger.maybe_compact:302-306 acquires the lock and IMMEDIATELY
     releases it, purely as a detection probe to avoid spawning a redundant child.
     It is the only acquire/release pair not used for mutual exclusion, so the
     shared helper must stay cheap and side-effect-free beyond the file.
   - Real acquire/release call sites: enrich_drain.drain :328 / :376;
     compact_trigger.run_sweep :223 / :265.

7. POST-STOREPATHS STATE (the risk the task flagged): NO stale symbol found.
   The plan named no _rebar_dir helper, so nothing it cites was removed by
   6f18-05de-beaf-42be. Confirmed the modules now go through StorePaths:
     src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:42        StorePaths(tracker).sidecar(...)
     src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:50-59  sidecar/log derivations
     src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:65-77       <store>/gc/ derivations
   git log --oneline -5 confirms the StorePaths commits at HEAD:
     3406014085 Prove the store-path guard flags, not just passes
     55e308eaaf One StorePaths derivation for store sidecars

8. CITED TICKETS - all resolve; canonical ids recorded.
     COMMAND: rebar show <alias>
     nuclear-calm-heron            -> da68-fc7c-068c-4c53  closed  bug
     knavish-stimulated-bluebottle -> aadc-9af6-0e67-4e2a  closed  bug
     6f18-05de-beaf-42be           -> closed  story (the dependency; landed)
     airborne-wellloved-kingfisher -> 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a  in_progress  epic

================================================================================
BASELINE VERIFICATION RUN
================================================================================
COMMAND:
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py \
    tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py \
    tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q
OUTPUT:
  80 passed in 184.37s (0:03:04)
These are the pinning suites. They are green on the current tree, so any failure
after the consolidation is attributable to the change.

Also confirmed the ORIGINAL AC 1 fails today as intended (2 hits, but only 2 of
the 3 copies):
  COMMAND: grep -rn "O_EXCL" src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py \
             src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py
  OUTPUT:
    src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:126
    src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:143

================================================================================
OTHER CHANGES TO THE PLAN
================================================================================
- Preserved the "## Guard construction" section verbatim.
- Preserved the ACCEPTED RACE comment (enrich_drain.py:135-163, operator decision
  2026-08-16) as an explicit instruction to move it verbatim into the new module;
  deleting it would silently drop an operator ruling.
- Made the net-LOC criterion executable rather than a bare instruction:
    git show --numstat HEAD -- src/rebar | awk '{a+=$1; d+=$2} END {print a-d}'
- Description trimmed to 7798 bytes for the plan-review admission limit; the
  review-remediation log that was in the description now lives in this file.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The "O_EXCL-create a lock file, write a v2 owner stamp, reclaim once if stale" loop exists **three**
times, not twice:

- `llm/enrich_drain.py:98-170` `_acquire_advisory_lock` (73) / `:173-178` `_release_advisory_lock`
- `_commands/compact_trigger.py:119-160` `_acquire_trigger_lock` (42) / `:163-173` `release_trigger_lock`
- `_snapshot/gc_trigger.py:109-145` `_acquire_worker_lock` (37) / `:148-158` `release_worker_lock`

Each opens `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)` inside `for attempt in
range(2)`, adjudicates with `rebar._store.lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale(path)`, unlinks and
retries once on a stale verdict, then writes `lock_owner._owner_stamp()`. The copy spread the
unresolved-path defect (`nuclear-calm-heron` = `da68-fc7c-068c-4c53`, closed) and was called a third
dialect by `knavish-stimulated-bluebottle` (`aadc-9af6-0e67-4e2a`, closed). Dependency
`6f18-05de-beaf-42be` (closed) landed: all three derive paths from `StorePaths`/`_gc_dir`; no `_rebar_dir` helper remains.

### The copies are NOT identical
1. **Same:** the ceiling (all call `stamped_file_is_stale(path)` bare; sole ceiling
   `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S = 3600`, `lock_owner.py:46`) and the retry cap `range(2)`.
2. **Release semantics — the one real behaviour delta; FIX it, do not propagate it.**
   `_release_advisory_lock` (`enrich_drain.py:174-178`) wraps `os.close(fd)` and `os.unlink(...)` in
   ONE `try`, so an `OSError` from `close` SKIPS the unlink and leaks the lock until the ceiling. `release_trigger_lock` (`compact_trigger.py:164-173`) and `release_worker_lock`
   (`gc_trigger.py:149-158`) use TWO independent `try` blocks, so the unlink always runs. **The
   shared implementation MUST use the two-block form** — a deliberate, tested change to the drain.
3. **Stamp bytes.** Drain appends `"\n"` (`enrich_drain.py:165`), the others do not
   (`compact_trigger.py:156`, `gc_trigger.py:142`) — invisible, both readers `.read().strip()`
   (`lock_owner.py:349-350`, `doctor_locks.py:279-280`). Adopt no-newline.
4. **Logging.** Drain names the holder via `_describe_drain_lock_holder`
   (`enrich_drain.py:129-134`, helper `:74-95`) and warns on a failed stamp (`:167-169`); the others
   log bare (`compact_trigger.py:147`, `gc_trigger.py:132`) and swallow the stamp failure. The
   drain's holder phrasing is pinned to `doctor`'s wording by
   `test_enrich_drain.py:585::test_drain_and_doctor_describe_a_holderless_lock_identically` and
   **must survive**. Adopt the drain's stamp-failure WARNING everywhere (logging superset).

## Approach
Extract `src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py` beside `lock_owner.py`, which stays the staleness
authority (the new module has no staleness logic of its own):
- `stamped_file_lock(path, *, label, describe_holder=None) -> int | None` — O_EXCL create, stamp
  write, single stale-reclaim, reclaim WARNING (drain passes `_describe_drain_lock_holder`, the
  other two `None`), stamp-failure WARNING, and the ACCEPTED RACE comment moved verbatim from
  `enrich_drain.py:135-163` (operator decision 2026-08-16 — a ruling that must not be dropped).
- `release_stamped_lock(path, fd) -> None` — the **two-independent-`try`** close+unlink.

**Directory creation stays with the callers** — the mechanisms differ: drain and compaction
`os.makedirs(StorePaths(tracker).rebar_dir, exist_ok=True)` returning `None` on `OSError`
(`enrich_drain.py:118-122`, `compact_trigger.py:135-139`); GC uses `_gc_dir`'s
`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (`gc_trigger.py:65-69,122-125`). The helper takes a resolved
`path: str | os.PathLike[str]` (GC passes `Path`).

**Guard anchor: `os.O_CREAT` ∧ `stamped_file_is_stale`, NOT `O_EXCL`.** A bare `O_EXCL` scan
over-matches 7 legitimate lines (`_signing_hmac.py:100,104`, `_store/fsutil.py:13`,
`opcert_service/keyprov.py:122`, `llm/code_review/registry.py:385`, `doctor_locks.py:49,249`), and
`O_EXCL` ∧ `stamped_file_is_stale` still matches `doctor_locks.py` — the diagnostic READER (real
call `:304`, opens WITHOUT `O_CREAT` at `:119`).

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner
module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition
count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour
pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Constraints
- `compact_trigger._acquire_trigger_lock` and `release_trigger_lock` are monkeypatched **by name as
  module attributes** at `tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py:134-135` with **no
  `raising=False`** — both must stay module-level attributes of `rebar._commands.compact_trigger`
  or that test errors. They and `gc_trigger.release_worker_lock` are PUBLIC; no renames. All six
  are called directly by the three worker test modules.
- `doctor_locks` reads these stamps (`:101-103`, `_existence_report` `:248-317`, `scan_locks`
  `:320-370`): stamp bytes must stay `.strip()`-equivalent.
- `compact_trigger.maybe_compact:302-306` acquires then immediately releases as a **detection
  probe**, not exclusion — the helper must stay cheap and side-effect-free beyond the file. Other
  call sites: `drain` `:328`/`:376`; `run_sweep` `:223`/`:265`.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py` (new), `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py`, `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py`,
`tests/unit/store/test_stamped_lock.py` (new).

## Testing
New tests: acquire / second refused / release / re-acquire; a stale stamp
(`monkeypatch.setattr(lock_owner, "_pid_alive", lambda _pid: False)`) reclaimed exactly once, third
collision `None`, live stamp never reclaimed; stamp parity; release-on-close-failure; the drain's
holder WARNING. The pinning suites named in the Acceptance Criteria are green today (80 passed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No `src/rebar` module outside `stamped_lock.py` performs the acquire; checked by
  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/store/test_stamped_lock.py -q` and by
  `grep -rlF "os.O_CREAT" src/rebar --include="*.py" | xargs grep -lF "stamped_file_is_stale" | grep -v "^src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py$"`
